extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, electric cooperative leaders, regulators, and industry stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Policy and operational guidance for ensuring electric grid reliability and affordable service for electric cooperatives and their members, including recommendations on generation mix, permitting, supply chain, funding, and emergency response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affordability and reliability as core policy goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Policymakers must approach national energy policy with affordability and reliability at the core while also balancing aspiration with reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy should prioritize keeping the lights on and costs families and businesses can afford; balance long-term climate goals with short-term ability to deliver reliable, affordable power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow time, technology development, and transmission build-out
rubrics_metrics.description: Policymakers must recognize the need for time, technology development and new transmission infrastructure before taking our nation down an energy path that prioritizes speed over practicality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transitions require realistic timelines and infrastructure planning; avoid policies that force premature retirements or underbuild transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a diverse supply of always-available energy technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: NRECA supports efforts to maintain a diverse supply of always available energy technologies that are essential to keeping the lights on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include baseload and dispatchable resources (e.g., coal, natural gas, nuclear, hydro) alongside renewables to ensure capacity and firming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for substantially increased generation capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Achieving net-zero economy-wide emissions by 2050 could require generation capacity to increase by as much as 480% compared to what is in place today.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Energy planning must account for large increases in capacity needs driven by electrification; model and provision for that demand when setting policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fuel diversity to ensure reliable, affordable, responsible supply
rubrics_metrics.description: Electric co-ops rely on a diverse energy mix to ensure a reliable, affordable and responsible electricity supply that meets the needs of their consumer-members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-ops should explore all options, technologies and ideas; policy should not mandate one-size-fits-all generation mixes given local differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'disorderly' retirement of existing generation assets
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'disorderly' retirement of existing generating assets is directly impacting reliability; many assets taken offline have been replaced with sources providing less capacity or intermittent resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retirements should be orderly and replacements must provide equivalent capacity and reliability; assess capacity contributions of replacement resources before permitting retirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitting reform to expedite generation and transmission projects
rubrics_metrics.description: The current permitting process required to build, site and maintain electric generation and transmission infrastructure is outdated and a significant impediment to meeting tomorrow’s energy needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streamline regulatory reviews, reduce timelines (examples: SPEED Act, PERMIT Act), and limit litigation delays; recognize a single transmission project can take up to 10 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for transmission expansion needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Electrifying other sectors could require a threefold expansion of the transmission grid by 2050.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and planning should include major transmission build programs and remove barriers that slow siting and interregional connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address supply chain delays and resilience
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply chain delays are contributing to an unprecedented shortage of the basic machinery and grid components essential to ensuring continued reliability of the electric system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize domestic production, faster procurement, and inventory strategies; example: distribution transformer lead times increased from an average of 70 days to 340 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure availability and resilience of natural gas as baseload/backstop
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. is increasingly reliant on natural gas for baseload power and as a backstop for intermittent generation sources; availability has been challenged by extreme weather events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies should preserve reliable natural gas supply chains and fuel security, especially for winter/peak events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect hydroelectric resources (e.g., Lower Snake River dams)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hydroelectric power is a reliable, abundant source of electricity; agreements that jeopardize dams threaten reliability and increase costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rescind policies or MOUs that risk breaching dams that supply significant hydropower to regional co-ops; factor regional hydro reliance into federal decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support RUS funding and loan programs for co-ops
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-ops need increased funding for RUS loans to provide more power and meet extraordinary demand for investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Congress should boost funding for Rural Utilities Service programs to accelerate co-op projects for generation, transmission, distribution, and broadband.

rubrics_metrics.name: FEMA reform and improved disaster assistance mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: FEMA reform is needed so co-ops can access timely assistance after disasters to restore reliability and protect members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streamline FEMA programs, clarify eligibility (e.g., Category F public assistance), and ensure co-ops can obtain rapid aid for storm recovery and resilience investments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wildfire mitigation and grid hardening investments
rubrics_metrics.description: Sound land management policies and grid hardening investments will help combat wildfires and support reliable service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund and implement vegetation management, system upgrades, and community-specific mitigation without one-size-fits-all federal prescriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitting timelines and NEPA modernization
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental impact statements must be completed within two years; new permitting procedures should speed approvals for co-op projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative and administrative reforms should set firm timelines and reduce duplicative reviews to accelerate projects while preserving necessary environmental review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve start-of-construction rules for energy tax credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Treasury should keep start-of-construction rules for energy credits to avoid forcing co-ops to scrap projects or incur more debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain stable tax and incentive rules to prevent project uncertainty and financial harm to co-ops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor permitting and regulatory programs to site-specific circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should finalize permitting programs that can be tailored to individual sites rather than 'one-size-fits-all' rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations (e.g., coal ash) should allow flexibility for site-specific permitting to avoid undue compliance burdens and reliability impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure EPA and other rules consider reliability impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA power plant rules and similar regulations should be assessed for their impact on grid reliability and consumer costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory reviews should include reliability assessments and cost impacts; NRECA argues some rules are 'unlawful, unrealistic and unachievable.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy flexibility to reflect co-ops’ diverse resource mixes
rubrics_metrics.description: Every cooperative’s resource mix is unique and will continue to vary depending on assets, costs, reliability implications, and local circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policymakers should provide long-term certainty and flexibility so co-ops can adopt solutions that fit local needs and minimize undue harm to rural/low-income consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support deployment and scaling of energy storage
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest among electric co-ops in deploying energy storage is growing and should accelerate as more experience is gained, costs decline, and battery performance improves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage demonstrations, incentives, and policies that facilitate adoption of storage technologies suitable to co-op needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in community-scale microgrids for remote reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE funds for co-op microgrids will improve reliability and economy in remote communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support targeted funding and pilots for microgrids in isolated or disaster-prone areas to maintain service continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize production of critical grid components domestically
rubrics_metrics.description: Senators introduced bills to boost U.S. transformer production; ensuring domestic supplier capacity is vital for security and reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote policies (funding, incentives, procurement preferences) to increase domestic manufacturing of transformers and other grid-critical equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect low-income assistance programs (LIHEAP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lawmakers should ensure that federal staffing cuts do not mean that LIHEAP comes to a halt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain funding and administration capacity for programs that help vulnerable members afford electricity during transitions and crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate regulation for transmission on federal lands
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear bureaucratic and legal barriers that add burdensome delays and increase costs for transmission projects on federal lands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Congress should help streamline approvals, reduce duplicative requirements, and coordinate agencies to facilitate timely projects connecting renewable generation to load centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mutual aid, drones, and logistics planning in emergency response
rubrics_metrics.description: Crews, contractors, and logistics planners use mapping, drones, parts inventories, and plotted work plans to restore service rapidly after disasters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency preparedness should include prepositioned supplies, vendor relationships for expedited resupply, mutual aid agreements, and phased rebuild strategies to restore service to most-populated areas first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance emissions reductions with consumer cost and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-ops have reduced emissions through efficiency and renewables but forcing premature shutdowns of coal or gas plants would raise rates for consumers who can’t afford increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy should aim for emissions progress compatible with affordability and reliability, including support for carbon capture R&D and regionally appropriate zero-emission sources like hydro and nuclear where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocate for streamlined agency procedures and constructive federal actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Smart federal policies, streamlined permitting rules, and agency efforts can help bring megawatts onto the grid to meet rising demand from data centers, electrification and manufacturing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage agencies (DOE, RUS, Corps) to align funding, technical assistance, and regulatory processes to accelerate co-op projects.
